newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open weaker on Thai baht fallout.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open weaker on Thai baht fallout.

text.p: Singapore shares opened weaker on Friday as the market felt the shock waves rippling through the region from Thursday's Thai baht crisis, dealers said.
"We're still being affected by the turmoil in the currency markets," one dealer at a local firm said.
"Confidence is being wiped out," said another.
Dealers said the baht had more impact on the market than Singapore's weak first quarter economic data released on Friday.
At 0230 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index slipped 15.51 to 2,054.23. Volume was a slim 34.2 million shares and losers swamped gainers 167 to 48.
Banking and other blue chip stocks again the major casualties, but dealers said bargain hunting could return after the sell down.
"There's an opportunity to buy while prices are at rock bottom -- but don't get over invested," one dealer said.

Early actives were again led by newly-listed Poh Lian Holdings with 2.4 million shares traded to stand down Singapore S$0.005 (US$0.003) at $0.515. Shares in Hong Fok Corp were suspended pending an announcement.
Singapore Press foreign fell S$0.70 at S$27.80 while OCBC foreign slipped S$0.40 to S$17.50.
